statement:
The line $L_1$ has vector equation
$$\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\2\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}2\\2\\-3\end{pmatrix}.$$
The line $L_2$ has vector equation
$$\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}4\\-2\\9\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\-2\end{pmatrix}.$$

Show that the distance $D$ between a point on $L_1$ and a point on $L_2$ can be expressed in the form
$$D^2=(3\mu-4\lambda-5)^2+(\lambda-1)^2+36.$$

Hence determine the minimum distance between the two lines.
solution:
A general point on $L_1$ is $(1+2\lambda,\,2\lambda,\,2-3\lambda)$ and on $L_2$ is $(4+\mu,\,-2+2\mu,\,9-2\mu)$. The squared distance between them is
$$D^2=(3+\mu-2\lambda)^2+(-2+2\mu-2\lambda)^2+(7-2\mu+3\lambda)^2.$$
Expanding and collecting,
$$D^2=17\lambda^2-24\lambda\mu+38\lambda+9\mu^2-30\mu+62=(3\mu-4\lambda-5)^2+(\lambda-1)^2+36.$$

Since squares are non-negative, $D^2\ge36$, and equality is achieved when both squares vanish, i.e.
$$3\mu-4\lambda-5=0 \quad\text{and}\quad \lambda-1=0.$$
The second gives $\lambda=1$, and then $3\mu-4-5=0$ gives $\mu=3$.

Therefore the minimum distance is $D_{\min}=\sqrt{36}=6$.
hints: Write a general point on each line using the parameters.
Compute the squared distance and expand it.
Complete the square to see the minimum is 36, attained when both squares are zero.
